Application Materials.content:
Typically, postgraduate applicants should supply relevant supporting documents, but should consult school webpages for any specific or additional requirements.
- **Proof of previous degree(s):** usually an academic transcript and certificate. If you have not yet graduated, upload your most recent transcript showing results to date. If studying qualifications from outside the UK, also include documents indicating the marking scheme used.
- **Official English translations:** if certificates or transcripts are in a language other than English, include official, authenticated English translations with the original documents. The translation should state it is accurate and include the translator/translation company contact details, credentials or qualifications, date of translation, and full name and signature.
- **Academic references:** for postgraduate taught courses, most applications will not require references. Sometimes one or two references are requested in the application or assessment process. If requested, references should normally be from academic staff at university-level institutions; one employer reference may be used if you have been out of education for the last two years. References should normally be dated no more than two years before the course start date, at least one should be from your most recent institution if you studied at more than one, and referees should not be family members. Uploaded references **must be signed, dated and on official letterheaded paper**.
- **English language certificates (International applicants):** the certificate from the test provider/awarding body confirming you have been awarded the qualification.
- **Supporting statement:** for most postgraduate taught courses, a supporting statement is not required, although you may be asked about your motivation for studying the course. Where a personal statement is required, supply a statement of **at least 300 words** giving your reasons for applying and any other information in support of your application, such as how your previous education and experience relates to the course and how the course fits your long-term academic or career plans.
- **Curriculum vitae (CV)/resume:** you may wish to supply a CV or resume, particularly if you have professional experience relevant to the area you want to study.
- **Examples of work:** some courses may ask for samples of written work or a portfolio of artwork; where required, information will be included on the course webpages.
Supporting documents can be attached to the online application when applying or later by [logging back into the application](https://www.sheffield.ac.uk/postgradapplication). Upload high quality scanned colour copies or colour photographs showing the full document, including all text, images and security features. Clear, colour photographs or scans of original qualification documents must confirm the qualification has been awarded, show the date of award, and show the final awarded grade.

Academic Requirements.content:
- **Minimum 2:1 undergraduate honours degree in any subject.**
- You do **not** need to have studied data or analytics before to study this course.
- Applications are assessed “on the basis of the applicant’s preparation and achievement as a whole.” The university “may accept applicants whose qualifications don’t meet the published entry criteria but have other experience relevant to the course.”
- If required degree subjects and modules are listed, these are indicative only; Sheffield may accept subjects or modules that are not listed, and may not accept listed subjects or modules, depending on the content studied.
- For Chinese university degree holders: you will usually need a **4 year bachelor's degree** from a recognised university in a relevant subject for entry. Most postgraduate courses require a UK 2:1 or equivalent; the score required depends on the university attended and the course applied to.
| Chinese university category | Grade equivalent to UK 2:1 | Grade equivalent to UK 2:2 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Top 100 + Project 985 + Project 211 + Double 1st Class | **70%** | 65% |
| ARWU 101-300 | **75%** | 70% |
| ARWU 301-500 | **80%** | 75% |
| ARWU 501 upwards + All other Universities, independent and Private Colleges recognised by ECCTIS | **85%** | 80% |

**IELTS 6.5 (with 6 in each component)** or University equivalent. [Other English language qualifications we accept](https://sheffield.ac.uk/postgraduate/english-language "English language requirements for postgraduates")
#### Pathway programme for international students
If you're an international student who does not meet the entry requirements for this course, you have the opportunity to apply for a pre-masters programme in [Science and Engineering](https://usic.sheffield.ac.uk/programmes/pre-masters/science-and-engineering) or [Business, Social Sciences and Humanities](https://usic.sheffield.ac.uk/programmes/pre-masters/business-social-sciences-and-humanities) at the [University of Sheffield International College](https://usic.sheffield.ac.uk/). This course is designed to develop your English language and academic skills. Upon successful completion, you can progress to degree level study at the University of Sheffield.

Program Overview.content:
The MSc Business Analytics is offered by the Management School, Faculty of Social Sciences. The course starts in September 2026, lasts **1 year**, and is **full-time**.
The complex business challenges of today need managers with the analytical and technical skills to tackle them. Students gain skills including the use of Python and data visualisation, and explore how to apply them to decision-making within a business.
Making effective decisions is crucial in today’s business world. This course will develop the skills needed to analyse complex business challenges and make decisions that have a positive impact. Students do not need to have studied data or analytics before; the course starts with fundamentals and progresses to complex analytical models, decision-making and independent research.
The course uses links with industry to bring guest lecturers to the course, and students work with real-world data sets to put skills into practice. Working with industry experts helps students develop knowledge of working with stakeholders to understand their needs. For the project dissertation, students can choose to work with an organisation to gain more industry experience and apply course theory to a real-world challenge.
The Management School is Triple Crown accredited by [AMBA](https://www.associationofmbas.com/), [EQUIS](https://www.efmdglobal.org/accreditations/business-schools/equis/) and [AACSB](https://www.aacsb.edu/).
Teaching methods include lectures, seminars, tutorials and computer-based laboratories. Assessment methods include exams, essays, projects, portfolios, lab sessions and tests, presentations, and a dissertation project.
The course includes an industry-focused capstone project, desirably conducted in collaboration with business partners, where students apply analytical skills to solve practical business problems and gain real-world experience.
Students graduate with knowledge and experience for a career in business analytics, gaining hands-on skills such as Python programming for data analysis and automation, data wrangling, statistical modelling and basic predictive analytics, mathematical programming and optimisation for business decision-making, data visualisation using tools like Power BI, Tableau or Python libraries, database management and data governance principles, business problem-solving using analytics tools, decision support systems and scenario analysis, communication of data insights, and project-based learning through the Capstone Project.
Possible career pathways include Business/Data Analyst, Analytics Consultant, Data Scientist, Operations/Supply Chain Analyst, Marketing/Customer Insights Analyst, Risk/Financial Analyst, Business Intelligence, Product/Strategy Analyst, and Supply Chain/Data Coordinator. These roles could be based in industries such as consulting, finance, retail, logistics, tech, healthcare and government.
Dr Emilia Vann Yaroson, Lecturer in Operations and Supply Chain Management in the Management School, is listed as an academic involved in the programme.

Financial Aid.content:
International Postgraduate Scholarship 2026: scholarships worth **£3,000** are available to overseas fee-paying students starting their studies in **September 2026**. The scholarship is awarded automatically as a tuition fee discount to eligible students with no additional application required. **The deadline for applications to this scholarship has now passed.**
Eligibility:
- You must commence your studies of a postgraduate taught degree at the University of Sheffield in **September 2026**.
- All courses are eligible, with the exception of those listed.
- You must accept your offer from the University of Sheffield before **4pm (UK time) on Tuesday 7 July 2026**.
Further information:
- The scholarship will be awarded automatically if you accept your offer to study at the University of Sheffield before **4pm (UK time) on Tuesday 7 July 2026**; no additional scholarship application is required in the first or any subsequent years.
- The scholarships will take the form of a tuition fee reduction only.
- You must be self-funded and classified as overseas for tuition fee purposes.
- The scholarship cannot be awarded in conjunction with any other scholarship or discount offered by the University unless explicitly stated.
- The scholarship is for full-time and part-time students only. Students studying online or via distance learning are not eligible.
- Part-time students will receive the full-time equivalent of the scholarship split pro rata over the duration of the Masters course, subject to all eligibility and award criteria.
- If you are studying a 2-year masters programme the scholarship will be available in the second year of your studies subject to successful completion of year 1.
- This scholarship cannot be deferred to a future year of entry.

Multiple Applications.content:
Part 2 is where you select the course or courses you want to apply for. **You can apply for a total of three different postgraduate courses.**
If you want to apply for more than one course, you don't need to submit them all at the same time. Each course choice has its own 'Submit Application' button.

Deferral Admission Policy.content:
If we've offered you a study place and you will be unable to attend at the start of your course, you may be able to defer your entry to the next admission point. Most postgraduate taught courses have one admission per year, at the start of the autumn semester in September/October.
For most courses, you can request a deferral through [your original online application](https://www.sheffield.ac.uk/postgradapplication) by clicking on the 'Request Deferral' link in the 'Your Applications' section. Requesting a deferral will deactivate your current offer, so you should only request one when you're sure that you can't start on the original start date. If you aren't sure, the University advises submitting a new application for the next admission point, when applications open for that year.
If the academic selectors approve your request, the University will send you an amended offer letter with a deferred start date. You should submit your deferral request by the deadline published on the [key dates](https://sheffield.ac.uk/postgraduate/deadlines "Key dates and deadlines for postgraduate courses") webpage.
You can ask to defer your application for a **maximum of two academic years from your original start date**. If you want to defer beyond that, the University will ask you to re-apply. Deferral requests are reviewed by admissions selectors, then the University will let you know the decision. The University can't always review deferral requests when they receive them, and can't issue deferred offers until after the new admissions year has begun, usually in September. Receipt of the request will be acknowledged within two weeks.
